paper_metadata.title: Effects of Solution Treatment on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Ti-22Al-25Nb Alloys

evidence.section: 3.2. Effects of Solution Temperature and Time on Microstructures
evidence.quote: After the a2/B2 solution treatment at 1 010 and 1 030 C, it is clear that numerous equiaxed a2 particles are distributed in the interior and at the boundary of the B2 grains (Figure 2a,b). With the increase in the solution temperature, the volume fraction of the a2 phase significantly decreases from approximately 7% (Figure 2a) to almost 0 (Figure 2d).

evidence.quote: Room temperature tensile tests were performed on an ISTRON 1195 electronic universal testing machine at a constant strain rate of 10-3 s-1. The specimens were manufactured with a 10 mm gauge length and 30 mm total length. Here, the axial direction was parallel to the rolling direction of the sheet, and the yield strength (YS), ultimate strength (UTS), and elongation (EL) were measured.

mechanisms.name: dislocation pile-up
mechanisms.material_state: solution-treated at 1010 C for 120 min, water-quenched

evidence.quote: During the process of tensile deformation, massive dislocation pills up at the grain boundaries, and it is difficult for dislocations to penetrate. This local pill up of dislocation along the grain boundaries results in stress concentration and, thus, reduce the ductility significantly.
The nominal composition of this alloy, which was fabricated by pack-rolling at 1 000 C, was Ti-22Al-25Nb (at%).

evidence.quote: As mentioned above, the a2 particles that pin the grain boundary cause a local grain boundary discontinuity and, thus, prohibit the grain boundary motion (Figure 2f). In addition, it is seen in Figure 3 that several B2 grains grow faster than the surrounding grains. The above results prove that the B2 grain growth behavior of the Ti-22Al-25Nb alloy is mainly controlled by AGG.
